title: Synthetic acceptance and rejection tests for the Expedition verifier core
summary: Five frozen synthetic tests established the verifier core's normalization, acceptance, rejection, empty-input, and unknown-challenge behavior without disclosing the sealed Expedition answer.
why_run: To establish deterministic verifier behavior as a precondition for packaging Expedition 001.

pipeline.description: Construct a temporary synthetic challenge manifest and exercise normalization, match, nonmatch, empty input, and unknown-ID paths.

output.summary: All five frozen verifier-core tests passed.

acceptance.criterion: Five specified synthetic test cases complete successfully.

controls: The positive vector must match its generated SHA-256 digest.
The negative vector must not match.
No XPD-0001 answer is stored in the tests.
interpretation: The frozen verifier core behaved as specified under the public synthetic control suite.
limitations: Unit tests establish deterministic core behavior, not desktop usability.
The sealed XPD-0001 acceptance test is performed privately against the packaged candidate.
This is not Liber Primus source evidence or a plaintext claim.

normalization_changes: Converted the flat public record into the canonical run-package schema.
Preserved the original five-test execution separately from later repository test-suite growth.
No measured output or claim was altered.

raw_artifacts.reason: No separate historical test log was preserved; the exact summarized output remains in the canonical output object.
